pairs.question: Conceptusne mihi tandem, partusque futuros, Sancte, refers? mene attactus perferre viriles posse putas? cui vel nitenti matris ab alvo protinus inconcussum, et ineluctabile votum virginitas fuit una: nec est cur solvere amatae jura pudicitiae cupiam, aut haec foedera rumpam?
pairs.answer: Immo istas (quod tu minime jam rere) per aures foecundam Spiritus alvum influet, implebitque potenti viscera partu, flammifero veniens caelo, atque micantibus astris.
pairs.derivation: Mary's entire reply to the angel is one extended question challenging how she could conceive while remaining a virgin; quoted contiguous and verbatim (1.183-188) as the question, with first-word capitalization kept and terminal punctuation normalized to '?'. The answer is the angel's operative first sentence: I stripped the mid-line speech tag 'excipit interpres' (narration of speaking, lines 189-190) and began the answer at 'Immo' ("on the contrary"), which directly answers that the Spirit, not male contact, will make her fertile. The window ends at the first full stop after 'astris' (line 192); what follows ('At tu, virgineum mirata...') turns to predicting her wonder and the proof of Elizabeth's pregnancy, i.e. elaboration, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Dicite, pastores (neque enim sine numine, credo, tam certum tenuistis iter), cui tanta paratis munera? cui virides ramis frondentibus umbras texitis? anne aliquis superum Patre missus ab alto has docuit sedes, locaque haec accedere jussit?
pairs.answer: Nova per tenebras, nova lucis imago, o genitor, media visa est modo lumina silva spargere, et in nostras diffundere gaudia mentes: sive Deus caelo veniens, seu forte Deorum nuntius, in dubio est: nos vultum, habitumque loquentis vidimus: et motas per noctem audivimus alas.
pairs.derivation: Joseph's whole speech to the shepherds (3.1133-1137) is one contiguous question asking for whom they prepare gifts and whether some heavenly being sent them ('anne aliquis superum... has docuit sedes'); quoted verbatim and contiguous, terminal punctuation normalized to '?'. The answer is the shepherds' reply: I stripped the framing tag 'Illi autem:' (narration, line 1139) and kept their words from 'Nova...' The reply directly answers 'who sent/taught you' by describing the apparition of light that directed them, noting it is uncertain whether a god or a messenger. The default window runs to the first full stop, which is at the end of 'alas.' (line 1144), so the whole reply is one answering sentence-span; the next text ('Sic fati, jungunt dextras...') is narration and is cut.
